temporal_state_chain.observed: Ethan notices Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep; Ethan invites Gary to a weekend relaxation retreat, but Gary declines, saying there is too much to do at the hospital.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is a dedicated friend/doctor whose excessive hospital work is putting his health at risk, and he hopes a retreat can help Gary rest.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes — Gary's refusal confirms/refines that Gary is heavily overcommitted and not yet willing or able to step away from work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary remains dangerously overworked and resistant to taking a break, so the problem is serious and ongoing.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To keep trying to help Gary rest and find a way to intervene or support him despite the refusal.

temporal_state_chain.observed: During the retreat, Ethan observes that Gary is restless and avoids discussing work.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is overworked by hospital obligations and needs relaxation, but he has not yet suspected a deeper personal cause.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes — Gary's restlessness and avoidance make Ethan suspect that Gary's overwork is not only about professional obligations and that Gary may be hiding something.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes there is more to Gary's overworking than just hospital duties; Gary may be dealing with an unspoken personal or emotional problem.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To gently confront Gary and encourage him to open up without judgment.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After the confrontation, Gary opens up about the pressures of managing a new department and personal challenges he is facing.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan suspects Gary is hiding something and that the overwork involves more than professional obligations, but he does not know the specifics.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes — Gary's disclosure explains the overwork and confirms Ethan's suspicion; Ethan now understands the professional and personal pressures Gary faces.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary's actions are understandable given his new-department pressures and personal challenges, and that Gary needs both empathy and practical help to find balance.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To help Gary find a better work-life balance by prioritizing tasks and delegating responsibilities.

temporal_state_chain.observed: Over the following months, Ethan regularly checks in with Gary; Gary reports progress and remaining challenges, including that he has less overwhelm and had time for a movie.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary is beginning to address his work-life balance with help, but likely still needs ongoing support and encouragement.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes — Gary's reports show real improvement and use of support, while also showing that challenges remain.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is making meaningful progress toward a healthier balance and is becoming less overwhelmed.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To continue offering support, encouragement, and regular check-ins.

temporal_state_chain.observed: After a year, Gary has successfully adjusted to a healthier work-life balance; he says he feels more in control and thanks Ethan for his support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_before: Ethan believes Gary has made progress but may still benefit from regular check-ins and support.
temporal_state_chain.belief_update: Yes — Gary's successful adjustment and self-reported control show that he can now manage independently.
temporal_state_chain.belief_after: Ethan believes Gary is self-sufficient and has achieved a healthier balance, no longer needing close intervention.
temporal_state_chain.emotion: Satisfied and happy for his friend.
temporal_state_chain.intention: To step back while letting Gary know he is always available if needed.
